name: Virunga National Park
blurb: Mountain gorillas, volcanoes and hippos: forest, savanna and lake in one rift.

tip.title: Bring back the hippos
tip.text: Hippo dung feeds tilapia. Lower hippos and watch tilapia, then the fish eagles and crocodiles that depend on them.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Virunga National Park

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Podocarpus and other trees make up the montane forest on the volcano slopes, giving leaves, bark and fruit to monkeys, apes and elephants.

nodes.name: African alpine bamboo
nodes.desc: A bamboo belt grows on the volcano slopes at roughly 2,300 to 2,600 m. Gorillas move into it when fresh shoots appear.

nodes.name: Galium vines and forest herbs
nodes.desc: Galium vines are available all year in the high forest and are a staple food of mountain gorillas.

nodes.name: Savanna grasses
nodes.desc: Sacaton and other grasses cover the lava and Rutshuru plains and feed the large grazers of the lowland savanna.

nodes.name: Lake phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Microscopic algae in Lake Edward turn sunlight and dissolved nutrients into food for fish such as tilapia.
A black-and-white leaf-eating monkey of the forest canopy. Chimpanzees and leopards prey on colobus monkeys.

nodes.name: Eastern chimpanzee
nodes.desc: An omnivore that eats mainly fruit and leaves and also hunts monkeys such as colobus. Present in the park forests.

nodes.name: African bush elephant
nodes.desc: Grazes and browses on the savanna. Seeds from caper and wild cucurbit plants pass through its dung balls, spreading plants across the grassland.
Rests in the lake and rivers by day and grazes on land at night. Its dung feeds tilapia, so falling hippo numbers hit the fishery.
A big grass-eating herd animal of the central sector savanna, and a main prey of the lions there.

nodes.name: Uganda kob
nodes.desc: Thomas's kob is the abundant antelope of the Lake Edward plains. It grazes short grass and feeds lions, leopards and hyenas.
A hunter and scavenger on the savanna, feeding on kills and on carcasses such as dead hippos.
A fish-eating raptor that perches along the lake shore and snatches tilapia from the surface.
Lives along Lake Edward and the rivers. It eats fish, takes antelope at the water's edge and scavenges carcasses.
The park and Queen Elizabeth National Park in Uganda form one lion conservation unit. Lions need healthy kob and buffalo populations.
A secretive forest and savanna hunter of monkeys, antelope and apes. Silverback gorillas defend their groups against it.
Light on the open lake and the savanna drives the growth of algae and grass.
Eruptions of Nyiragongo and Nyamuragira spread ash and lava that weather into fertile soil for forest and grass.

nodes.name: Fungi, insects and microbes
nodes.desc: Break down dead leaves, dung and carcasses and return nutrients to the volcanic soil.
